parts.text: But I’m NOT relieved
parts.meaning: But I do not feel better

parts.text: knowing that our time on Earth—the time of Earth—is going to be very, very, very short
parts.meaning: because I know that our time, and the time of the world, will be very short

parts.text: if we don’t act quickly.
parts.meaning: if we do not do something fast.

sentences.grammar: "Knowing that ..." gives the reason. "If" + present ("if we don't act") is used for a real future possibility. The capital letters in "NOT" show strong feeling.

sentences.context: I’m terrified because I know exactly what I have to do next.
sentences.simple: Jack is very afraid, because he knows what he must do.
sentences.main: I’m terrified.

parts.text: because I know exactly what I have to do next.
parts.meaning: because I know just what I must do now.

sentences.grammar: "Because" gives the reason. "What I have to do" is a noun clause: the thing that I must do.

sentences.context: He’s served his purpose, so we could just let him free—but I’m worried that he’ll get his brains sucked out by the tree.
sentences.simple: They do not need Alfred anymore and could let him go, but Jack is afraid the tree will eat his brain.
sentences.main: I’m worried that he’ll get his brains sucked out.

parts.text: He’s served his purpose,
parts.meaning: We do not need him now,

parts.text: so we could just let him free—but
parts.meaning: so we could let him go, but

parts.text: I’m worried that he’ll get his brains sucked out by the tree.
parts.meaning: I am afraid the tree will suck out his brains.

sentences.grammar: "Serve your purpose" = do the job you were needed for. "Get + something + past participle" ("get his brains sucked out") = something is done to it, often something bad.

sentences.context: And this monster was just plucked from its home and happened to land here.
sentences.simple: The worm was pulled from its world and came here by chance.
sentences.main: This monster was plucked from its home.

parts.text: And this monster was just plucked from its home
parts.meaning: And this monster was taken from its home

parts.text: and happened to land here.
parts.meaning: and by chance landed here.

sentences.grammar: "Was plucked" is passive: someone or something did it to the monster. "Happen to + verb" = do something by chance.

sentences.context: If he gets his hands on the bestiary, he only needs to bring it to the tree.
sentences.simple: If Thrull takes the book, all he must do is carry it to the tree.
sentences.main: He only needs to bring it to the tree.

parts.text: If he gets his hands on the bestiary,
parts.meaning: If he takes the monster book,

parts.text: he only needs to bring it to the tree.
parts.meaning: he just has to take it to the tree.

sentences.grammar: "If + present, + present" shows what will happen. "Get your hands on" = get or take something. "Only needs to" = that is all he must do.

sentences.context: I pride myself on being a cool, calm, never-panicked hero—but right now I’m way far from that.
sentences.simple: Jack is proud that he is usually a calm hero, but now he is not calm at all.
sentences.main: I pride myself on being a cool, calm hero.

parts.text: I pride myself on being a cool, calm, never-panicked hero—but
parts.meaning: I am proud that I am a cool, calm hero who never panics, but

parts.text: right now I’m way far from that.
parts.meaning: now I am not like that at all.

sentences.grammar: "Pride yourself on + -ing" = be proud of something about yourself. "Way" is informal and makes "far" stronger.

sentences.context: You must understand—even though we all came here from the same world, we know each other no better than you might know a stranger whom you encounter.
sentences.simple: Bardle says that the monsters came from the same world, but they do not know each other well, like strangers.
sentences.main: We know each other no better than you might know a stranger.

parts.text: You must understand—even though we all came here from the same world,
parts.meaning: Please understand: although we all came from the same world,

parts.text: we know each other no better than you might know a stranger whom you encounter.
parts.meaning: we do not know each other better than you know a stranger you meet.

sentences.grammar: "Even though" shows a surprising contrast. "No better than" = not better than. "Whom" is the object form of "who"; it is formal, which fits Bardle's old way of speaking.

sentences.context: It seems to be leaking darkness, like the place itself cannot stand light.
sentences.simple: The forest seems to give out darkness, as if it hates light.
sentences.main: It seems to be leaking darkness.

parts.text: It seems to be leaking darkness,
parts.meaning: Darkness seems to be coming out of it,

parts.text: like the place itself cannot stand light.
parts.meaning: as if the forest hates light.

sentences.grammar: "Seem to be + -ing" = look like it is doing something. "Cannot stand" = hate, cannot accept. "Itself" adds force: the place, not just the trees.

sentences.context: I’ve learned that I am, apparently, a terrible judge of character in monsters.
sentences.simple: Jack has found out that he is bad at knowing which monsters are good and which are bad.
sentences.main: I am a terrible judge of character.

parts.text: I’ve learned that
parts.meaning: I have found out that

parts.text: I am, apparently,
parts.meaning: it seems I am

parts.text: a terrible judge of character in monsters.
parts.meaning: very bad at telling which monsters are good people.

sentences.grammar: "Apparently" between commas = it seems so (from what happened). "A good/terrible judge of character" = someone who is good/bad at knowing what people are really like.

sentences.context: Thrull no longer looks defeated—no, he looks like he’s on his last legs, forced to demonic desperation.
sentences.simple: Thrull does not look beaten. He looks almost finished, and so he is ready to do anything, however evil.
sentences.main: Thrull no longer looks defeated.

parts.text: Thrull no longer looks defeated—no,
parts.meaning: Thrull does not look beaten now. No,

parts.text: he looks like he’s on his last legs,
parts.meaning: he looks almost finished,

parts.text: forced to demonic desperation.
parts.meaning: so desperate that he will do something evil.

sentences.grammar: "No longer" = not anymore. "No," in the middle corrects the first idea with a better one. "On your last legs" = very weak, almost finished.

sentences.context: But even a post-apocalyptic action hero can’t keep them safe all the time.
sentences.simple: Even a hero after the end of the world cannot always protect his friends.
sentences.main: A hero can’t keep them safe all the time.

parts.text: But even a post-apocalyptic action hero
parts.meaning: But even an action hero after the end of the world

parts.text: can’t keep them safe all the time.
parts.meaning: cannot protect them always.

sentences.grammar: "Even" shows something surprising: not even a hero can. "Keep + someone + adjective" = make them stay that way.

sentences.context: I had hoped if the monsters could keep Thrull busy, we could do him in with the Weed-B-Gone.
sentences.simple: Jack hoped that while the monsters fought Thrull, they could kill him with the weed killer.
sentences.main: I had hoped we could do him in.

parts.text: I had hoped
parts.meaning: I hoped before this

parts.text: if the monsters could keep Thrull busy,
parts.meaning: that, if the monsters kept Thrull busy,

parts.text: we could do him in with the Weed-B-Gone.
parts.meaning: we could kill him with the weed killer.

sentences.grammar: "Had hoped" (past perfect) shows a hope that did not come true. "Keep someone busy" = give them things to do. "Do someone in" is informal: kill them.

sentences.context: Only the space marine suit keeps me from being blown to bits.
sentences.simple: Jack is not broken into pieces by the explosion only because he is wearing the armor suit.

parts.text: Only the space marine suit
parts.meaning: Just the armor suit, nothing else,

parts.text: keeps me from being blown to bits.
parts.meaning: stops me from being broken into pieces.

sentences.grammar: "Keep someone from + -ing" = stop it from happening. "Being blown" is a passive -ing form. "Only" at the start means nothing else saved him.

sentences.context: Quint’s so happy to be a regular that he’s just making up new regular rules as he goes.
sentences.simple: Quint is so happy to be a regular customer that he keeps inventing new rules for regulars.

parts.text: as he goes.

sentences.grammar: "So + adjective + that ..." shows a cause and its result. "Make up" = invent. "As he goes" = while he is doing it, without planning.
